- Model consistently underestimates true price spikes, especially after bullish sentiment events or high supply net events — adjust forecast upward by 2–5% for such contexts.
- When sentiment is bullish (≥0.67) and supply net is negative, model tends to lag — add 1–3 days of upward momentum to forecast.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model overcorrects downward — cap downward slope at 1–2% per day to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and supply net is negative, model underreacts — increase downward slope by 0.5–1.5% per day.
- For 30-day forecasts, mean reversion is weak — if 2+ consecutive days show downward trend, model should not assume continuation; instead, allow 1–2% upward correction if sentiment shifts bullish.
- When official events are high volume (≥20 events/30d) and supply net is negative, model underestimates true price — add 3–5% to forecast baseline for such contexts.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to smooth transitions — introduce 1–2% volatility buffer in forecast to reflect sentiment swings.
